summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: EWA grows despite legal limbo
articles.description: Instant Financial and Clair are among the earned wage access companies expanding even as state and federal oversight evolves.

articles.title: Visa delivers 6M documents to DOJ
articles.description: The government and the card network will need to complete their pre-trial evidence work by the end of January, a magistrate ruled Friday.

articles.title: Beyond the booking: How Navan scaled global card issuing with embedded finance
articles.description: How Navan unlocked €1B+ in card volume by embedding global issuing with Adyen.

articles.title: Modernizing payments is a must
articles.description: “Payments modernization is no longer a future aspiration,” writes one bank tech executive. “It has become an operational and strategic imperative.”

articles.title: Illinois seeks to support cash use
articles.description: A new state law will require retailers to accept cash for most transactions below $500, and fine repeat violators up to $5,000.

articles.title: Card fees have staying power
articles.description: Merchants keep attacking the fees, but the charges keep coming because consumers love swiping their cards.

articles.title: Is the nickel nearing a revamp?
articles.description: It costs 13 cents to produce the five-cent coin. Congress wants the U.S. to explore more cost-effective methods.

articles.title: RTP gears up for int’l reach
articles.description: The Bank of New York and other financial institutions are preparing for a pilot next year that will stretch the real-time payments network across borders.
